hook: A long, heavily styled piece presented as files received from another timeline, and it plays with what you think you know about the canon. Knowing a few of the site's most famous entries pays off, but the less you know about this one going in, the better. There is an accessibility mode if the visual effects get in the way, and some later scenes are intense.
whyItMatters:
SCP-6820 is the first episode of a series called Admonition, and its tags connect it to a wide web of established lore: groups of interest, old AIs, antimemetics and the noosphere. It is a co-authored, illustrated work that treats the wiki's shared history as raw material, reusing well-known items as tools inside its plot.

Its unusual esoteric object class signals early that it will not follow the standard format.
thingsToNotice:
The opening puzzle, a weapon built to erase something nobody can recall and a lingering hatred with no target, drives the whole piece, and the clues (reptilian traits, acid, adaptation) let you solve it before the staff do. Watch the small fragments tacked onto the ends of sections; together they form a second voice running under the document.

The termination attempts double as a tour of other articles, including the terse pointer from SCP-2719. The ending flips the format completely, collapsing into an obsessive, warped rewrite of a very familiar containment file, which makes the erased subject's return its final blow.

related.note: Knowing this classic is close to essential for the reveal.
Its concept pointer reappears here as one of the attempted tools.
Brought in near the end as an antimemetic countermeasure.
